newsitem.title: UK: Newcastle Utd flotation to raise 47.4 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: Newcastle Utd flotation to raise 47.4 mln stg.

text.p: Broker NatWest Markets said on Friday it was offering ordinary shares on behalf of British soccer club Newcastle United Plc at between 120p and 135p each.

NatWest said the offer aimed to raise 47.4 million stg net of expenses and valued Newcastle United at between 172 million stg and 193 million stg. Dealing in the shares was expected to start on Wednesday, April 2.
Newcastle United, currently third in England's Premier League, said in January it aimed to raise up to 50 million stg in the flotation, joining the nation's growing league of listed soccer clubs.

Britain's soccer sector has expanded strongly in recent years, leaving behind the hooligan-plagued 1980s to become a multi-million pound leisure industry keen to promote itself as family and business-oriented. Eight of England's 20 premier league clubs are either listed or planning to float.

"Approximately 21 million stg will be used to repay borrowings, approximately 12 million will be used to pay for future instalments of transfer fees for current players and up to 10 million will be used to fund the proposed training and youth team development facilities," non-executive chairman Terence Harrison said in a statement.

NatWest said a minimum 10 percent of the 40 million new ordinary shares would be set aside for the general public and the remainder for financial institutions. Newcastle posted a trading loss of 23.9 million after transfer costs in 1996 on turnover of 28.97 million. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 4017
